Package dev.opencollab.paletter.block

Class ResolvedBlock

java.lang.Object
dev.opencollab.paletter.block.ResolvedBlock
public final class ResolvedBlock extends Object
A block state resolved against one palette: what it sends for it and what that does, see Palette.resolve(dev.opencollab.paletter.vanilla.BedrockBlockState). A palette makes a resolution once per state and keeps it, with its BlockValues handle; states that resolve alike may share one. Use Palette.runtimeId(dev.opencollab.paletter.vanilla.BedrockBlockState) where only the id is needed. Resolutions are equal if they have the same definition, kind and behaviour (a handle of the same block in the same palette); compare them with equals.
Since:
1.0.0

  • Method Details

    • definition

      public @NonNull RegisteredBlockState definition()
      The block this resolution sends.
      Returns:
      the block to send, with its fallbacks applied, see Palette.blockDefinition(dev.opencollab.paletter.vanilla.BedrockBlockState)
      Since:
      1.0.0

    • kind

      public @NonNull ResolutionKind kind()
      How the palette resolved the state for its version.
      Returns:
      ResolutionKind.EXACT (also for a block asked for by runtime id), ResolutionKind.ADAPTED (the same block with state values fitted to the version), ResolutionKind.FALLBACK (a BlockFallback, also a forced one), ResolutionKind.DEFAULT (the default fallback block) or ResolutionKind.MISSING (no fallback at all: air is sent)
      Since:
      1.0.0

    • fallback

      public boolean fallback()
      Whether the block sent is a replacement.
      Returns:
      true if the state has no block of its own in this version, or is forcibly replaced: kind() is FALLBACK, DEFAULT or MISSING. Not for a state that is only adapted to this version's state values
      Since:
      1.0.0

    • behaviour

      public @NonNull BlockValues behaviour()
      The behaviour of the block sent.
      Returns:
      the behaviour values (friction, destroy time, collision shape, ...) of definition() in the palette that resolved it
